newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian plane crashes with no survivors.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian plane crashes with no survivors.

text.p: A Nigerian Boeing 727 airliner missing since Thursday evening has crashed with no survivors, an aviation ministry official said on Friday.
"All the 141 people that were on the plane died," she said, adding that Aviation Minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh had gone to the crash site.
Udo-Imeh told state television that search teams found the wreckage of the plane in a Lagoon at Egbin northeast of Lagos.
"The aircraft plunged into a lagoon," he said.
He said he did not know if there were any survivors.
Flight ADC086 operated by Aviation Development Company, a privately owned airline, lost contact with the control tower in Lagos at 5 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Thursday minutes before it was due to land.
The plane was flying from the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt to Lagos with 132 passengers and nine crew members.
Witnesses said scores of relatives of people believed to have been on board had assembled at the offices of the airport authority and many were weeping.
Military ruler General Sani Abacha expressed shock at the crash, saying he prayed "Almighty God to grant the families of the passengers the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss."
"The head of state also prayed God to grant the deceased eternal rest," said a statement from the presidency in the capital Abuja, the first official statement on the crash.
The search for the aircraft with the help of the police and airforce on Friday has been long and hard because of the wide area the police said they had to cover.
At a point the police issued a statement appealing to people all over southwestern Nigeria to look out and report any sighting of the wreckage.
"All farmers, fishermen, travellers, hunters and local people within neighbouring states should alert the police as soon as the aircraft is found," the statement said.
ADC declined further comments on the incident, referring all enquiries to the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria.
"It is a sensitive national issue and we are all tensed up here," a spokesman for the agency said, declining to speak further on the incident.
Airport sources said it was unusual for a plane to have been missing for so many hours without trace.
They said several foreigners were on board, possibly oil company executives.
Local newspapers said some expatriate staff of commodity trading firm, E D & F Man Limited, were also said to be on board.
ADC had not released a passengers' list more than 24 hours after the plane disappeared.
Its offices in the Ikeja suburb of Lagos were besieged all night by worried relatives of people thought to be on board.
Economic troubles have weakened Nigeria's infrastructure in recent years and there has been a spate of air disasters.
ADC is fully owned by Nigerian shareholders. It operates domestic services and also flies to some West African countries. One of its planes crashed in Liberia last year.
It shares fell 20 kobo on the Nigerian stock market to 4.40 naira in reaction to the crash.
In January a presidential jet crashed in the north killing Abacha's son and 13 others. Another crash in Jos, central Nigeria in June killed a state military governor and several other officials.
